All ten also handle the basic Tabs, Combobox and single-dialog flows, so the split comes from Dialog robustness. A, B, I, J and D keep a stack of open dialogs, capture the opener before React autofocuses a child, and support clearing the Combobox to null, so focus return and Escape stay correct when dialogs are nested or contain autoFocus content. F, E and H override autoFocus children and drop focus to body on close; I confirmed the bug the inspector reported for H, and it also affects C, E, F and G, where their inspectors missed it. G and C additionally break nested dialogs, and C cannot clear the Combobox to null. Among the top group, the differences are minor polish: B, D and J trap so strictly that focus cannot reach a portal rendered inside the dialog, and A's prop surface is narrower.

Beyond those, the ranking comes down to proportion and fit. I and D are compact and exact, normalize stored amounts and lock correctly. ranking.rationale: Clean and fully correct single-threaded, with good context isolation. But the spec's 'refunds never add up to more than its total' plus idempotency keys (a retry/concurrency feature) is broken under concurrent calls, the one major defect in the field.

judges.verdict: J is the only build without a lock. I confirmed real over-refunds (9 of 200 trials) and RuntimeError crashes under ordinary thread scheduling, so it is clearly last. The other nine meet the spec at the default decimal context. They differ on proportion and on smaller edge cases. I and D are correct, compact and thread-safe. C is the cleanest code, but it writes the key before a step that can fail, which corrupts the ledger under a lowered decimal precision. A, B, G, H and F are correct but over-engineered for this small codebase, and F also keeps refund state in a global registry.
